title: Reading and Writing Files
instructions: Programs can save data to files and read it back later, so information survives after the program ends.
The steps are always: open, use, close.
- fopen("notes.txt", "w") opens a file for writing ("w"), creating it if needed.
- fprintf(file, "...") writes into it, just like printf but aimed at the file.
- fopen(..., "r") opens for reading, and fgets reads a line back.
- fclose(file) closes it. Always close what you open.
task: Add the fprintf that writes "Hello from C!" into the file, so it prints:  the file said: Hello from C!
hint:
Write to the file with fprintf:

    fprintf(f, "Hello from C!\n");
expected_output: the file said: Hello from C!
